Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:

- Policy stance (FOMC 9/21/22): Hawkish. Target range raised to 3–3.25% with guidance for ongoing hikes and continued balance-sheet runoff, tightening both short-end rates and term/liquidity channels.
- SLOOS (July 2022) credit supply: Banks tightened standards and terms for C&I loans (large, middle-market, small firms), CRE loans, most residential mortgage categories (GSE-eligible, jumbo, subprime), HELOCs, credit cards, and subprime auto; banks also increased loan costs and collateral requirements for C&I. Banks cited the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and liquidity as key reasons.
- SLOOS demand: Stronger demand for C&I (including foreign banks) and HELOCs, and from small firms; weaker demand across CRE categories.
- Macro/market implications: Fed tightening plus bank-side tightening in SLOOS points to a sharper contraction in credit availability and higher borrowing costs—amplifying downside risks to growth and investment. Strong labor data and pockets of loan demand provide some offset, but the balance skews more negative for near-term activity, even as disinflation prospects and policy credibility improve over time.

Net tone: More negative than baseline given simultaneous policy tightening and bank credit tightening indicated by SLOOS.
